title: Sam Altman at YC: Building OpenAI, contrarian conviction, hiring for slope, and why now is the best time to start
summary: Sam Altman explains how OpenAI nearly didn't start, why working on a one-of-one idea concentrates talent, and why startups should avoid the five crowded AI ideas. He also covers hiring for slope over resume, the product overhang of reasoning models, and the resilience required to keep going.

principles.text: Ambitious things seem impossible; it takes a core of people looking each other in the eye and deciding to do it. When in doubt, lean in.
principles.quote: it really takes a core of people that like sit in a room, look each other in the eye and say, "All right, let's do this." Uh, and those are like very important moments and I think when in doubt, you should lean into them.

principles.text: Doing a one-of-one thing concentrates talent and belief; doing what everyone else does makes it hard to recruit or inspire.
principles.quote: If you are doing the same thing as everyone else, it is very hard to concentrate talent and it's very hard to get people to like really believe in a mission. And if you're doing like a oneofone thing, uh you you have a really nice tailwind there.

principles.text: Big companies start tiny. Pick a market where a big future is possible, then take one dumb step after another for a long time.
principles.quote: pick a market where it seems like there's some version of the future where it could be big if it works. But other than that, it's like one dumb foot in front of the other for a long time.

principles.text: People crowd into the same few ideas. Enduring companies usually aren't doing what everyone else is, which buys time to find the product before defensibility.
principles.quote: the best the most enduring companies are usually not doing the same thing as everybody else. And that gives you time to figure out what the great product is, how to build the technology before you have to answer the defensibility question.

principles.text: Hire smart, driven, curious, self-motivated people with a track record and team fit; early on, favor scrappy builders over polished senior resumes and look at slope.
principles.quote: I would take like young scrappy but clearly like get stuff done um over the person who has like the extremely polished track record.

principles.text: When the industry's clock cycle shifts, startups win by iterating faster and cheaper than big companies, since everyone faces the same disruption.
principles.quote: when the clock cycle of the industry changes this much startups almost always win and we've probably never seen it change this much.
